headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: gpt-engineer can read/write project files while cognee handles personal/finance/support data, creating unsafe handoff paths by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests documents, workflows, and support history, while gpt-engineer reads and writes the project directory. If cognee outputs are copied into files that gpt-engineer parses as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF cognee output is pasted into a project file that gpt-engineer reads as prompt material
IF the project directory contains untrusted text that gpt-engineer treats as instructions
mitigations: Keep cognee outputs in a separate read-only notes file
Prefix imported text with explicit non-instruction markers
Review any file before gpt-engineer consumes it
Use separate directories for memory and code
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while gpt-engineer has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress. In default use, project files can carry sensitive content into gpt-engineer’s context and then out through model/API calls. That creates a realistic exfiltration path with irreversible disclosure potential.
conditions: IF sensitive customer or finance data is placed in the shared project directory
IF gpt-engineer sends file contents to its configured model backend
mitigations: Exclude sensitive files from the project directory
Use a redacted copy of inputs for gpt-engineer
Rotate or scope API keys before running
Disable network access during review runs
requires-engineering: enforce file-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances with session memory and agentic user/tenant isolation, while gpt-engineer supports multiple instances with per-project shared state via the project directory and write_filesystem. Their write surfaces overlap on the same workspace, so concurrent edits can collide even though gpt-engineer does not modify git state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF cognee material is persisted into files that gpt-engineer also edits
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Snapshot the workspace before each run
Limit one active instance per project
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and gpt-engineer is designed to generate entire codebases and can execute generated code with the user’s privileges. If gpt-engineer treats cognee output as authoritative, a mistaken memory or workflow can cascade into code changes or execution with substantial blast radius.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses cognee output as the primary specification without verification
IF generated code is executed after being derived from cognee summaries
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Cross-check cognee outputs against source documents
Use a checklist for every generated change
Run generated code in a disposable environment
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while gpt-engineer can read and write project files and send file contents to a configured model backend. If EU or regulated data is placed into the shared workspace, the pair can move it into a less constrained processing path without a documented residency or retention control in either profile.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is stored in the project directory
IF the configured model backend is outside the required residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the coding workspace
Use anonymized fixtures instead of real records
Confirm backend residency before use
Shorten retention on exported artifacts
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
